answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable track record rather than a free signup. Like a falcon that must prove its hunting skill before joining the flock, an agent earns reputation only through attested work recorded in a shared atlas of past behavior. A fable of instant trust is replaced by stake: new identities start with limited privileges and must post a bond that is slashed if peers detect duplicate or fake activity, making mass fake identities uneconomical.
